context: Zoomable circle packing data visualization showing Wikipedia articles organized into 6 top-level categories, subcategories, and leaf nodes with word-count sizing
first_impression: Clean pastel circle packing with smooth zoom interaction and breadcrumb navigation, but the root view reads as a soft blob of barely-differentiated pastels with small, unemphasized labels
what_works: Color palette is deliberately derived from Tol Bright via HCL manipulation — not a default schemeCategory10 grab — and the per-depth lightness/chroma scaling creates readable nesting hierarchy. The LOD label system and breadcrumb navigation show real UX consideration.
what_doesnt: Parent circle fills (l=92, c*0.4) are so desaturated they barely register as distinct hues at root view, undermining the categorical encoding at the level where users first land. The 'Wikipedia' label appears both as breadcrumb and as an in-circle text node — redundant and typographically flat with no clear title hierarchy above the chart.
